title: Carried over from round 1 and not addressed (non-blocking): the expression [a.s…
description:
Carried over from round 1 and not addressed (non-blocking): the expression [a.stderr, a.stdout].filter((s) => s.trim().length > 0).join('\n').trim() is repeated verbatim at :86, :94, :117 and :128. A small local helper (e.g. combineStreams(res)) would remove the four-way duplication and give the stderr-first ordering a single point of definition. The jscpd dup gate passes as-is, so this is style only.

Source: cam/issue-363
Review round: 2

suggestion-fingerprint: fc4a19317501

spec.scope:
Harden the plan-preflight stderr surface shipped by CAM-363, as ONE coherent change. This issue is the UMBRELLA for CAM-368 + CAM-369 + CAM-370; all three are in scope here and the latter two will be closed as subsumed at ship.

Three coordinated parts:

(1) CAM-368 -- single definition point for the stderr-first ordering. src/supervisor/plan-preflight.ts:86, :94, :117, :128 each carry a byte-identical expression `[X.stderr, X.stdout].filter((s) => s.trim().length > 0).join('\n').trim()`. The stderr-FIRST ordering in that expression is now a LOAD-BEARING invariant (see gotcha 1), yet tests pin it at only 2 of the 4 sites (typecheck at test/supervisor/plan/plan-preflight.test.ts:255, bun-test at :314); a reversal at the git-checkout-main or git-pull site fails NOTHING today. Extract an EXPORTED helper `combineStreams(stderr: string, stdout: string): string` in plan-preflight.ts and call it from all four sites, so the ordering has one definition point and a single direct unit test covers all four. Export (rather than module-private, which is the file's own precedent via pruneMergedCamBranches) is REQUIRED so the helper can be unit-tested directly. The four bespoke per-site justification comments (L83-85, L93, L114-116, L124-127) collapse into one explanation on the helper; do not delete the reasoning, relocate it.

(2) CAM-369 -- real-boundary coverage for the production spawn closure. The sole production implementation of PlanPreflightSpawnFn is an inline, non-exported closure at src/commands/sidecar.ts:2638-2646 inside makeProductionPlanPhaseFn. It has ZERO test coverage: no test file imports or names preflightSpawnFn, and every unit test injects the string-returning fake at test/supervisor/plan/plan-preflight.test.ts:45-55. That closure is the EXACT seam where CAM-363's original stderr drop hid. Extract it into a NEW sibling module src/supervisor/plan-preflight-spawn.ts exporting `makePreflightSpawnFn(cwd: string): PlanPreflightSpawnFn`, have sidecar.ts import and call it (deleting the inline literal), and add a test that hits the REAL Bun.spawnSync boundary: spawn a real command that writes to stderr and assert the decoded string, plus assert cwd is honored. A test against a hand-copied equivalent closure does NOT satisfy this -- the repo invariant is to hit real I/O at wire boundaries.

(3) CAM-370 -- pin the both-streams-empty contract. When a failing step produces neither stdout nor stderr, detail is the empty string, which renders through truncatePreflightDetail as an empty tail: the marker/narration shows a step with NO verdict, which is the ORIGINAL SYMPTOM SHAPE that CAM-363 existed to eliminate. test/supervisor/plan/plan-preflight.test.ts:114-118 already constructs exactly that input (`{ exitCode: 1, stdout: '', stderr: '' }`) but asserts only `calls.length`. Pin the contract explicitly at the helper, at the runPlanPreflight result, and through the real truncatePreflightDetail.

OUT OF SCOPE, do not touch: the clean-tree step (plan-preflight.ts:106-108) stays stdout-only and byte-identical, deliberately, because git porcelain output has no stderr verdict; loopSpawnFn at src/commands/sidecar.ts:2628-2636, which carries the IDENTICAL stderr drop but is a different code path with a different type (LoopSpawnFn has no stderr field) and is deliberately deferred; and the required-ness of the `stderr` field on PlanPreflightSpawnFn, which must NOT be weakened to optional.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1 (CAM-368, single definition point): `grep -c 'filter((s) => s.trim().length > 0)' src/supervisor/plan-preflight.ts` returns exactly 1. It returns 4 on main, so this oracle fails today and can only pass after extraction.

AC2 (CAM-368, all four sites converted): `grep -c 'combineStreams(' src/supervisor/plan-preflight.ts` returns exactly 5 -- one definition plus the four call sites at the git-checkout-main, git-pull, typecheck and bun-test failure returns. A partial conversion (any site left inline) yields a different count and fails.

AC3 (CAM-368, helper is exported and directly tested): `grep -q 'export function combineStreams' src/supervisor/plan-preflight.ts` succeeds, AND test/supervisor/plan/plan-preflight.test.ts imports combineStreams by name from src/supervisor/plan-preflight.ts.

AC4 (CAM-368, ordering pinned at the definition point): a direct unit test asserts `combineStreams('ERRLINE', 'OUTLINE').split('\n')[0] === 'ERRLINE'`. Reversing the two operands inside the helper body must make this test FAIL -- verify that by actually reversing them locally, observing the red, and restoring before commit.

AC5 (CAM-368, single-stream cases): direct unit tests assert `combineStreams('', 'OUT') === 'OUT'` and `combineStreams('ERR', '') === 'ERR'` (no leading or trailing newline in either case, i.e. strict equality, not toContain).

AC6 (CAM-370, both-streams-empty contract) pinned at three levels: (a) `combineStreams('', '') === ''` strictly; (b) at test/supervisor/plan/plan-preflight.test.ts:114-118, extend the existing first-fail-only test (or add a sibling asserting on the same input shape) so that the runPlanPreflight result for a step failing with `{ exitCode: 1, stdout: '', stderr: '' }` asserts `result.ok === false` AND `result.detail === ''` strictly, in addition to the existing calls.length assertion; (c) `truncatePreflightDetail('') === ''`, exercised through the real imported function from src/supervisor/plan-preflight-marker.ts, not a reimplementation.

AC7 (CAM-369, closure extracted): a new file src/supervisor/plan-preflight-spawn.ts exists and exports `makePreflightSpawnFn(cwd: string): PlanPreflightSpawnFn`, typed against the PlanPreflightSpawnFn imported from src/supervisor/plan-preflight.ts (the type is NOT redeclared or widened).

AC8 (CAM-369, sidecar uses the extracted factory and no longer inlines it): `grep -c 'Bun.spawnSync(\[bin, ...args\]' src/commands/sidecar.ts` returns 0, AND src/commands/sidecar.ts imports makePreflightSpawnFn from src/supervisor/plan-preflight-spawn.ts, AND the value threaded as preflightSpawnFn into runProductionPlanPhaseWithReplan (currently sidecar.ts:2658-2660) is the result of calling makePreflightSpawnFn(cwd). The grep returns 1 on main, so it fails today.

AC9 (CAM-369, REAL boundary, no fakes): a test imports makePreflightSpawnFn from src/supervisor/plan-preflight-spawn.ts and calls the returned function against a REAL subprocess -- no injected fake, no hand-copied equivalent closure. It must assert all four of: (a) a command writing a known literal to stderr and nothing to stdout yields `stderr` containing that literal and `stdout.trim() === ''`; (b) a command writing to stdout and nothing to stderr yields the mirror result; (c) a command writing to BOTH streams yields both decoded, non-empty; (d) a non-zero-exiting command yields the matching non-zero exitCode. Bun.spawnSync must actually execute in every case.

AC10 (CAM-369, cwd is honored): a test creates a real temp directory, calls makePreflightSpawnFn(thatTmpDir), spawns a command that prints the working directory, and asserts the decoded stdout resolves to that temp directory. Passing a different cwd must change the result, so the assertion is not vacuous.

AC11 (out-of-scope guards, all three must hold): (a) src/supervisor/plan-preflight.ts still contains the exact line `return { ok: false, step: 'clean-tree', detail: status.stdout.trim() };`; (b) `git diff main -- src/commands/sidecar.ts` shows NO change to the loopSpawnFn body (the LoopSpawnFn closure that decodes only stdout remains byte-identical); (c) the PlanPreflightSpawnFn declaration still types `stderr` as a required `string`, not `stderr?: string`.

AC12 (file-size budget): src/commands/sidecar.ts NET LOSES lines from this change (the inline closure is deleted and replaced by an import plus a call), so its ceiling in scripts/file-size-budget.json must NOT be raised. If check:all reports the sidecar.ts ceiling as newly violated, that is a signal the extraction was not actually performed -- fix the extraction, do not raise the ceiling. Neither plan-preflight.ts nor its test files have budget entries; do not add any.

AC13 (gates): `bun run typecheck` zero errors, `bun test` zero failures, `bun run check:all` green. Total passing test count must be STRICTLY GREATER than main's 5179 (this change only adds test declarations; it removes none).
gotchas: TRUNCATION SURVIVAL is why the ordering is load-bearing, and it is the single most important fact in this spec. `detail` reaches the operator through truncatePreflightDetail (src/supervisor/plan-preflight-marker.ts:135-139), which renders FIRST LINE ONLY plus a ` (+N more)` suffix, and it is consumed at src/supervisor/plan-runner.ts:1607 for the `[cam] plan preflight failed: <step> - <detail>` narration. A stdout-first combination would bury the actual verdict (a TS error, a bun-test failure line) behind tens of kilobytes of banner chatter -- which is precisely what made the original incident undiagnosable. stderr MUST come first. Preserve that in the helper body.

The ordering is currently UNGUARDED at two of the four sites. Do not assume the existing suite protects you: test/supervisor/plan/plan-preflight.test.ts:120-129 (git-checkout-main) and :154-165 (git-pull) assert only `toContain(...)` with stdout empty, which passes identically under EITHER ordering. Only :255 and :314 use `.split('\n')[0]` and actually pin order. That asymmetry is the entire reason CAM-368 exists; the helper plus AC4 is what closes it.

ACCEPTANCE-CRITERION ORACLES MUST BE ABLE TO FAIL. The previous cycle shipped an AC whose shell oracle (a grep piped into another grep) could essentially never match, so it passed regardless of the code. For every grep-based criterion here, run it against unmodified main FIRST and confirm it currently FAILS, then implement and confirm it passes. AC4 in particular demands you actually reverse the operands, observe the red, and restore.

Do NOT weaken the required `stderr` field on PlanPreflightSpawnFn to optional to make anything easier. CAM-363 made it required deliberately, against the path of least resistance, because this repo has TWICE shipped bugs from test fixtures encoding a wrong process model (raw-echo.ts in CAM-359 and again in CAM-364). If a fixture does not compile, fix the fixture, not the type.

The fake at test/supervisor/plan/plan-preflight.test.ts:45-55 has a default-fill fallback returning `{ exitCode: 0, stdout: '', stderr: '' }` when its response array is exhausted. When adding the CAM-370 assertions, be sure the empty detail under test comes from the EXPLICIT failing response, not accidentally from that fallback.

src/supervisor/plan-preflight.ts is currently PURE and fully injectable -- it contains no Bun.spawnSync. Keep it that way: the new production factory goes in the NEW sibling module src/supervisor/plan-preflight-spawn.ts, never inside plan-preflight.ts. The flat sibling-module layout is the directory's own convention (44 flat domain modules, e.g. plan-preflight-marker.ts); there is no utils/helpers module in src/supervisor/ and you must not create one.

src/commands/sidecar.ts sits at 3437 lines against a ceiling of 3438 (one line of headroom, raised by CAM-363 for the r.stderr decode). This change must REDUCE that file. If you find yourself wanting to raise the ceiling, the extraction is wrong -- see AC12.

The extracted makePreflightSpawnFn must preserve the existing Buffer/TextDecoder guard shape exactly (`r.stdout instanceof Buffer ? new TextDecoder().decode(r.stdout) : ''`, and the same for stderr). Do not 'improve' it to `r.stdout.toString()` or similar; the guard handles the non-Buffer case that Bun's types permit.

macOS has no `timeout` binary. For the real-boundary tests, prefer spawning `bun -e '...'` or `sh -c '...'` for deterministic stream writes rather than relying on tool-specific output formats. Use a real temp dir (Bun/node tmpdir + mkdtemp) for AC10 and clean it up.

Do NOT run the full `bun test` suite repeatedly in parallel with other heavy work; the sidecar is live on this host. Scope test runs to the touched files while iterating, and run the full suite once at the gate.
domainTerms: plan preflight: the deterministic guard the plan runner runs before spawning the planner subagent (git checkout main, git pull, clean-tree, typecheck, bun test); a failure here halts the entire loop and writes .claude/.cam-plan-preflight-failed.json.
detail: the free-text failure payload on PlanPreflightResult, persisted into the preflight-failed marker and rendered to the operator FIRST LINE ONLY via truncatePreflightDetail.
stderr-first ordering: the invariant that combined stream output places stderr before stdout, so the actual verdict survives first-line-only truncation.
PlanPreflightSpawnFn: the injectable spawn seam used by runPlanPreflight; returns { stdout, stderr, exitCode } with stderr REQUIRED.
wire boundary: a seam where the code touches real I/O (subprocess, filesystem, tmux); the repo invariant is that such seams are covered by tests that execute the real thing rather than a fake.
